links.comparator_used: Current standard multi-reader (double reading) screening pathway, in retrospective simulation
links.outcome: Screening sensitivity, specificity, assessments and human reads
links.effect: Sensitivity +1.9-2.5%, specificity up to +0.6%, 4.6-10.9% reduction in assessments, 48-80.7% reduction in human reads (AI as second reader or high confidence filter)
links.tradeoff: Automation bias degrades performance in multi-reader settings (but improves it for single-readers); results are from retrospective simulation and need prospective studies before clinical adoption.
links.quote: Operating an AI reader as a second reader or as a high confidence filter improves current screening outcomes by 1.9-2.5% in sensitivity and up to 0.6% in specificity, achieving 4.6-10.9% reduction in assessments and 48-80.7% reduction in human reads.

design_hint: AI-integrated screening pathway design and triage filtering
